summary: This study compares sidestream smoke emissions from narghile (shisha, hookah) waterpipes and cigarettes, measuring ultrafine particles, carcinogenic PAHs, volatile aldehydes and carbon monoxide in a 1 m3 Teflon-coated chamber at 1.5 air changes per hour. A single waterpipe session emitted roughly four times the PAH and aldehydes, five times the ultrafine particles and about 35 times the CO of one cigarette in sidestream smoke. Including exhaled mainstream smoke, the authors estimate a waterpipe smoker produces ambient toxicants equivalent to 2–10 cigarette smokers, and argue waterpipe smoking should be included in public smoking bans.
one_line: Chamber study finding a single waterpipe session emits several times more ultrafine particles, PAHs, aldehydes and CO than a cigarette, supporting waterpipe inclusion in smoking bans.
key_facts: A single waterpipe use session emits in sidestream smoke approximately four times the carcinogenic PAH of a single cigarette, per the abstract.
A single waterpipe use session emits approximately 30 times the CO of a single cigarette in the abstract, while the discussion states about 35 times.
The waterpipe smoker likely generates ambient carcinogens and toxicants equivalent to 2–10 cigarette smokers during a typical one-hour waterpipe use session, depending on the compound.
Average ultrafine sidestream particle emissions were 3.99 ± 0.60 × 10^12 particles per waterpipe, versus 0.638 ± 0.188 × 10^12 particles per cigarette.
Count median diameter was 37.9 ± 4.1 nm for the waterpipe versus 132 ± 11 nm for the cigarette in the results section.
Carbon monoxide averaged 2269 ± 108 mg per waterpipe across 13 replicate sessions, versus 65.5 ± 5.5 mg per cigarette across 9 sessions.
The chamber was a 1 × 1 × 1 m Teflon-coated ageing chamber operating at 1.5 air changes per hour.

The waterpipe smoking protocol used a smoking machine programmed for 171 puffs of 2.6 s duration, 0.53 L volume, and 17 s interpuff interval, based on data from 52 waterpipe users in Beirut-area cafés.
Waterpipe tobacco used was 10 g of Nakhla brand Two Apples flavor ma'ssel; cigarettes were Marlboro Red tested under the Massachusetts intense protocol.
Total PAH per waterpipe was 1193 ± 226 ng, compared with 305 ± 49 ng per cigarette in the table.
Total aldehydes per waterpipe were 12,000 ± 1610 µg, compared with 2954 ± 416 µg per cigarette.
Formaldehyde emission per waterpipe was 5234 ± 1011 µg, compared with 357 ± 143 µg per cigarette.
The authors used absorption fractions of 70% for particle PAH, 60% for CO and 95% for aldehydes from Baker and Dixon (2006) to estimate exhaled mainstream emissions.
Charcoal was found to be a major contributor of ultrafine particles in waterpipe sidestream smoke at 5 minutes into a session.
The authors state that the study is limited to one tobacco and charcoal type, one smoking topography per product, and neglects chemistry changes from mixing sidestream and exhaled smoke.
